description: The four-level tree on the left has 7 nodes without value labels. The root's right child is a leaf. Its left child has two children: the one on the left is a leaf, and the one on the right branches into two more leaves.

A node's degree is its number of children. The right side labels this a “Full binary tree,” and a gray note below reads “Every node has degree 0 or 2.” All three non-leaf nodes have degree 2, and all four leaves have degree 0. No node has degree 1. The four leaves are spread across the second, third, and fourth levels.

frames.explanation: A full binary tree requires only that every node have zero or two children. The levels need not be full, and the leaves need not be at the same level.
frames.title: Full binary tree: every node has degree 0 or 2

summary: A full binary tree restricts the number of children per node without requiring every level to be filled.
title: Full binary tree: every node has degree 0 or 2
